doc.title: Tony Marino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 25, 2025

title: Using melody in bass solos (Overjoyed video)
summary: About a Bop Shop video, Marino says he quotes melody in solos like Phil Woods and Al Cohn did.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: There’s another video I saw, coincidentally close to me now at the Bop Shop.
And there’s a video of you playing first of all I’m going to take a guess at the song. I don't know if you remember the incident but I think you were playing Stevie Wonder’s “Overjoyed.”
Oh yeah. We played that, but I don’t remember playing that at the Bop Shop.
Well the reason I think you did is because you were, in your solo, playing little parts of the melody as if you were reminding everybody here’s the song in case you forget.

Yeah well I often do things like that because I can’t play eighth notes. I try to but I’m not near as good as a horn player or a piano player. So I use melody a lot in my solos you know I definitely – or try to make up a new melody off of it you know. But you know when you listen to Phil Woods or Al Cohn and the real tune masters, they used the melody very much as well. They definitely – the phrasing from the melody alone was a big part of their thing you know. [Inaudible] phrasing.
